title: David Organizes the Temple Workers
overview: As David nears the end of his life, he names Solomon king and organizes the Levites, the tribe set apart to serve at the place of worship, for work in the coming temple.

parts.label: Passing the crown (v. 1)
parts.note: David, old and near the end of his life, names his son Solomon as the next king. A fuller and messier account, including a rival claim by Solomon's brother Adonijah, is told in 1 Kings 1.

parts.label: Counting the Levites (vv. 2-5)
parts.note: David gathers the leaders and has the Levite men aged thirty and up counted, about four times as many as in Moses' day. He assigns them four kinds of work: running the temple, serving as officials and judges, guarding the gates, and making music on instruments David had provided.

parts.label: Organized by family (vv. 6-23)
parts.note: The Levites are grouped by descent from Levi's three sons, Gershon, Kohath and Merari, so each family had a clear place. Only Aaron's line became priests, while the sons of his famous brother Moses were counted as ordinary Levites.

parts.label: A younger starting age (vv. 24-27)
parts.note: In Moses' time the Levites carried the portable worship tent from place to place, but now worship has a settled home in Jerusalem, so David lowers the starting age to twenty. Why verse 3 says thirty is unclear, though it may reflect an earlier count made before this change.

parts.label: Helpers to the priests (vv. 28-32)
parts.note: The Levites assisted the priests by overseeing the courtyards and side rooms, purifying sacred objects, preparing the sacred bread and grain offerings, and keeping weights and measures. They also stood to give thanks and praise every morning and evening, and at the Sabbath, New Moon and yearly festivals.

think: What does it say about a community when it gives so much care and so many people to work most would never notice, like baking, measuring and keeping the doors?
